proposals.evidence: DEDR 3986(a) documents the pal tooth family: Kodagu pallï, Malayalam pallu, Tamil pal, Malto palu, Kolami pal, Gadaba pal/pallū with plural palkīl, and Toda pas̱. Survey plural and final-vowel material (including palku, pālkill, pāldu) remains unchanged. Toda parse is a comparative correspondence to its distinctive s̱ reflex; Betta Kurumba pallə extends the comparison to a lect absent from this article. Subsection (b) toothstick compounds are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 4935 gives Tamil/Malayalam muṭṭu knee and Kolami muḍsū/mūḍs knee. Survey muṭṭi/muṭṭə and muḍsu preserve their final vowels. Badaga muṭṭi is a comparative extension explicitly marked as a look-alike by the source, not a literal dictionary attestation. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 1514 directly gives Kodagu tittï, Kolami kis, Malto cicu and Toda tït fire. Badaga kiccə is supported indirectly by the article’s explicit identification of Toda kic as a Badaga loan; this proposal is for the Badaga source form, not for the borrowed Toda song word. Survey titta, kiss, cicadu and tīttə preserve their endings and transcriptions. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 5516 directly gives Brahui bining, Kolami vin- with past vint-, Kurukh mennā, Malto mene and Telugu vinu hear. Source cognacy identifies this family; surveyed Kolami vinti and Malto mēnpo retain their inflected/morphological endings. The Malto ending remains a comparative detail for review, not a claimed exact dictionary match. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
